Stop worrying. Be yourself. Show some interest in her hobbies. Respect her. If she likes you, she'll accept you for the person that you are. If not, move on.

Don't ask her out in the way you're thinking. Be casual, but confident and ask her to get dinner with you and have a specific and interesting place in mind. Something like, "hey do you want to grab dinner with me on Friday? There's this great traditional sushi bar place I've wanted to go to." Remember, informal = easy conversation, confident = you're the leader with the plan.

Don't go for goofy stunts that are more reserved for marriage proposals, go for easy, casual, cool. It's much easier for people to say "yes" when they don't feel pressured or uncomfortable, which a stunt would probably make her feel.

Don't think about it like, "THIS IS IT, THIS IS THE MOMENT WHEN I FIND OUT IF EVERYTHING IS GREAT OR EVERYTHING IS BULLSHIT!" and push the yes or no part, think about it like, "hey I want to do something with you, but if you're busy then it's cool i'll find something fun to do anyway". Low pressure, low stakes.

If she says yes then you've gotta work on your flirt game. Usually it's pretty simple, make sure she knows you're interested in being more than friends so she won't be sitting there analyzing everything you do to figure out if she's on a date or a friend-outing. Don't be gross about it. Compliment her in a way a platonic, not interested friend would not compliment her, but not in a way that's gross and an overreach. Something like, "wow your body looks amazing in that dress". A friend might say, "you look great" but they wouldn't say, "your BODY looks great" and it also adds a sexual subtext so she knows you're definitely interested in more. Don't shower her with compliments like those. Make them sparse, but genuine and meaningful.

The rest is just playing off your natural chemistry, assuming you have some there. Don't try to self-censor yourself and overthink everything you say, be genuine with your thoughts and words. People pick up on authenticity and they appreciate it. It also allows people to feel more comfortable around you because they feel like you're not hiding your actual thoughts and opinions from them.

Also, just for confidence boosters, go do something impressive and get really good at it, enough so that you're undeniably skilled at it. Being good at other things in life increases your confidence around others because you know they can't touch that part of you, no matter what they say, because you've already proven your worth to yourself. Plus it usually makes you more attractive to be really good at something cool like photography, rock climbing, playing a musical instrument, etc.
